ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All directors, officers, shareholders, and individuals with significant control must undergo pre-incorporation enhanced diligence against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, Canada's Special Economic Measures Act lists, the Criminal Code terrorist list, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals list, and domestic and foreign Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) databases. Continuous monitoring is required under FINTRAC's risk-based approach; any positive match triggers escalation, enhanced due diligence, and potential Suspicious Transaction Report filing under S.C. 2001, c. 41.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry – Service Alberta / NUANS Name Search System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be in English or French and set out in Latin script. For an unlimited liability corporation, the name must include a distinct element followed by 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' or 'ULC' as the legal element. Non-Latin script names must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet for NUANS search and registration; the distinct element must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing name or registered trade-mark in Alberta.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Director of Corporate Registry rejects a proposed name, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the Director within 30 days of the rejection notice, attaching a fresh NUANS report and a statement of the distinguishing features of the proposed name. Reconsideration is completed using the same statutory test under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta), R.S.A. 2000, c. B-9, s. 12. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may seek judicial review before the Court of King's Bench of Alberta.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible, provided the virtual office provider maintains a physical street address in Alberta at which process can be served during all business hours and receives corporate mail on behalf of the entity. A P.O. Box or mail-forwarding-only address is not acceptable. Payment processors Stripe and PayPal may require documented proof of a physical business address; a virtual office may be accepted if the company provides a remote-work statement and non-resident ownership declaration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: 0.5–1.0% annual probability of an unannounced on-site inspection for a low-risk, non-regulated stock-media company; 5.0–10.0% probability if the entity becomes subject to enhanced due diligence due to PEP/sanctions alerts, incomplete beneficial ownership documentation, or unusual transaction patterns.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, s 12(1) (Unlimited Liability Corporation)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation issued under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an Alberta Unlimited Liability Corporation; no escrow account or capital deposit requirement applies to share subscription proceeds.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the Corporation adopt its Articles of Incorporation as filed and confirm the issued share subscriptions set out in the share subscription register; that the registered office be fixed at [Calgary, Alberta address], and that [Name] and [Name] be appointed as directors of the Corporation. RESOLVED further that [Name] be appointed Chief Executive Officer, [Name] Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] Corporate Secretary, each to serve until replaced by the board; and that management is authorized to execute banking documents and take all necessary steps to complete formation. Approved this ___ day of ________, 20___.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS corporate name search through the online registry system or an authorized service provider. Submit a Name Reservation Request to secure the proposed corporate name for 90 days prior to incorporation. Include a distinct unlimited liability corporate designator such as 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' or 'ULC' in the name.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and ULC designator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, select alternate acceptable names and resubmit the amended name reservation request within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare Articles of Incorporation and Registration Forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry – Legal Entity Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and execute Articles of Incorporation under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, designating the company as an unlimited liability corporation. Attach the Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors. Ensure the registered office is situated in Alberta and each director has executed a signed consent to act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries the application, file corrected forms using an amendment to articles or a notice of change, and pay any applicable administrative correction fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit Filing and Obtain Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed incorporation package electronically through the Corporate Registry online portal. Pay the applicable state filing fee and receive the Certificate of Incorporation in downloadable PDF form after the registrar approves the application.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is delayed, request a status update using the filing receipt number and provide the registrar with the e-filing confirmation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Hold First Board Resolution and Appoint Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first organizing meeting of the board. Adopt the pro-forma first board resolution, ratify the share subscription and issuance to subscribers, approve the registered office address, appoint the officers, and authorize execution of banking documents. Record the proceedings in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Resolutions approving banking and registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any director dissents, convene an additional board meeting, pass a corrective resolution, and update the minute book before relying on the original resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register Municipal Business Licence and File Initial Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Calgary or City of Edmonton municipal licensing department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If a physical office or photography studio is established, apply for a general business licence. For a purely digital stock-photo platform without physical premises, confirm that no municipal licence is required. File any mandatory initial corporate records within 15 days of incorporation and maintain the registered office service address with the Alberta Corporate Registry.
required_dossiers: Business premises lease or occupancy details
AB registered office address for service
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal application is queried, provide the certificate of incorporation, occupancy permit, and safety inspection documents; appeal the decision to the municipal licensing board within 21 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing board applies to a pure digital stock-photo and generative visual asset platform
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating or manufacturing licence required; a municipal general business licence may apply only if physical premises are established

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – digital commercial stock-photo platform does not fall under mandatory Environmental Impact Assessment categories
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater or VOC effluent generated; electronic waste handling, if applicable, must comply with the Alberta Recycling Regulation (AR 60/2002) and applicable data-centre e-waste requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Where a physical office or studio is operated, a municipal fire safety certification, building occupancy clearance, and workplace safety approval under the Alberta Occupational Health and Safety Code are required; no such clearance is needed for a purely remote digital operation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada, including the My Business Account portal at https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html; Alberta corporate income tax is administered by the Alberta Treasury Board and Finance through CRA single-access registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Alberta ULC incorporated under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) must first obtain its corporate incorporation number from the Alberta Corporate Registry, then apply to the CRA for a federal Business Number (BN) through Business Registration Online (BRO) or by filing Form RC1, adding a GST/HST account if taxable supplies exceed the small supplier threshold. A non-resident ULC may register for a BN using a Canadian representative or agent; no minimum capital is required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a Canadian-resident ULC is taxed as a corporation on worldwide income, with foreign tax credits available, and is not a pass-through entity under Canadian federal or Alberta income tax law.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No domestic check-the-box election exists under Canadian income tax law; a ULC remains a taxable Canadian corporation for Income Tax Act purposes. Available elections include the ETA section 156 election among closely related corporations for GST/HST, ITA section 85 rollover elections on qualifying transfers, and amalgamation elections. For U.S. federal tax purposes only, a Form 8832 election may classify the ULC as a disregarded entity or partnership, but Canada does not recognize such election for Canadian tax characterization; hybrid mismatch rules under ITA sections 18.2 and 18.3 may apply.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) / Harmonized Sales Tax (HST); Alberta imposes no provincial sales tax, so only the federal 5% GST applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters (small supplier threshold); registration becomes mandatory once this threshold is exceeded, including for non-resident suppliers of digital services or intangible property to persons in Canada.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No national real-time e-invoicing, fiscal clearance, API clearance, or digital stamping mandate currently exists in Canada. GST/HST returns must be filed electronically using CRA GST/HST NETFILE, TELEFILE, or EDI/XML for prescribed large filers; supporting invoices must be retained for audit but are not cleared or digitally stamped by the CRA in real time.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods are zero-rated when sold by the supplier and exported by the recipient or by a common carrier to a destination outside Canada and possession passes in Canada solely for export. Services and intangible property, including digitized stock photos and AI-generated visual assets supplied electronically to a non-resident person, are zero-rated under Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act if the supply is made to a non-resident and is not for use or benefit in Canada and does not relate to real property or tangible personal property situated in Canada. The licensing of digital visual assets to non-residents is generally treated as a zero-rated supply of intangible personal property to a non-resident.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA Form B13A or equivalent electronic export report)
Bill of Lading, air waybill, or transport document evidencing export from Canada
Inward Remittance Certificate, bank FX confirmation (MT103), or equivalent evidence of repatriation of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess and claw back GST/HST previously zero-rated if documentary evidence fails to prove physical export or non-resident receipt and off-Canada use. False statements or omissions attract civil penalties under Excise Tax Act section 273 (up to 25% of the claimed refund plus interest) and general penalties under section 280.1, with criminal prosecution available for wilful evasion. Directors and officers may be personally liable under section 323. Retrospective assessment, interest, penalties, and denial of future zero-rating claims are standard enforcement consequences.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains an open capital account. The Canadian dollar is freely convertible on both current and capital transactions; no exchange control restrictions apply to commercial stock-photo royalties, dividends, or capital injections. Cross-border profit repatriation is subject only to Canadian withholding tax on dividends under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act, generally 25% absent a treaty reduction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canadian law does not impose surrender or mandatory conversion of export proceeds. Exporters may freely retain, convert, or disburse foreign currency via Canadian clearing channels.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. Offshore digital EMI providers (e.g., Wise, Payoneer, Stripe Treasury) are permitted as payment facilitators but cannot serve as a Canadian bank for regulatory capital clearing purposes. An Alberta ULC may use these for merchant collection and global payouts, but primary treasury accounts must reside with an OSFI-regulated Canadian bank to satisfy corporate governance and AML expectations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors must typically complete an in-branch or video-interview KYC where at least one authorized signing officer is identified in person or via secure video verification. A fully remote account opening is possible only for low-risk domestic entities with pre-existing valued relationships; non-resident shareholders increase the likelihood of physical attendance required by the major banks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: ULC pass-through status and unlimited shareholder liability may trigger enhanced due diligence on beneficial ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate record (Alberta Certificate of Incorporation, articles of amendment), full register of shareholders and directors, global ultimate beneficial owner listing, and audited financial statements if capital exceeds $100K.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High transaction velocity from digital stock-photo platform with disbursements to non-resident individual suppliers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: AML/CFT program tailored to low-risk digital merchant profile, transaction monitoring policies, contributor KYC policies, and evidence of platform-level fraud prevention controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound cross-border capital injections without bankable commercial justification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder resolution authorizing capital issuance, subscribed share purchase agreements, source-of-funds declaration, and prior-year balance sheet.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenue mix including royalty-like stock-image licensing may be misclassified as high-risk IP monetization.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Stock photography marketplace license agreements, platform payout statements, ISIC 7420 description of services, and tax-roll filings identifying intangible income.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer using SWIFT MT103 via an Alberta commercial bank account. No Canadian exchange-control submission is required; however, any cash flow exceeding CAD 10,000 must be reported to FINTRAC. Funds referencing 'Share Capital Contribution' should be accompanied by a board-resolution certificate and bank standard rep-and-warranty forms. Purpose narrative may state 'Contribution to working capital / capital increase' without statutory code.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments to global stock-photo contributors and content licensors are cleared via SWIFT MT103 (single payments), cross-border ACH batches, or commercial letters of credit (for high-value syndication contracts). For routine micro-disbursements, Stripe Connect and PayPal Business are integrated as supplementary rails, while standard payroll and supplier settlements use Lynx (CAD high-value) and CHIPS/Fedwire (USD) correspondent corridors.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla currency options (binary barrier excluded under Prudent Person Rule)
Offshore NDFs (used only for non-convertible minor currencies; CAD is fully convertible)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days after the anniversary date of incorporation or the previous annual return filing date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalties and potential administrative strike-off after two consecutive years of non-filing

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit required if the corporation has more than 10 shareholders, gross revenue for the prior fiscal year exceeds $1,000,000, or it is a subsidiary of a public company
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE)

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership and shareholding details required as part of annual return or upon any shareholding transfer
